mount.note: tilt and field of view measured together 2026-09-10 by scratch/depth_fit_models.py: the lidar's beams projected into the depth image agree best at 78 deg / 26 deg (residual 1.2 %, 3.0 % at the nominal 70 deg / 28 deg). STALE twice over: those beams were projected at the lidar mount config/lidar.json carried that day, which a tape measure corrected on 2026-09-12 (the same self-calibration redone at the measured mount votes for a different camera, 76 deg / 35 deg, and 78/26 scores worse than it did); and the tilt and the field of view traded against each other in that fit, so a checkerboard that pins the focal length settles the field of view for good and leaves this tilt to be re-fitted live on the robot with the new fx held fixed.

notes: hfov_deg came from the lidar (78 deg, scratch/depth_fit_models.py, 2026-09-10), the AC310's nominal 70 deg placed the image's edges 8 deg wrong; a checkerboard calibration replaces it — run ros/calibrate.sh (print the board with --print), which writes an intrinsics block next to this one and sets calibrated: true. hfov_deg itself is never rewritten: it stays the nominal number pepin.camera.optics answers while calibrated is false (the block carries its own hfov_deg, derived from fx), so that boolean switches a bad calibration off and puts these optics back. The lidar that 78 deg came from was assumed 0.18 m lower than the tape measure of 2026-09-12 says it hangs, so that fit is owed a repeat: see the mount's note.
